title: Hetzner cluster topology
description: The whole per-environment description of one cluster. Loaded by infra/cluster from cluster.<stack>.yaml. Validation here is for the editor; pkg/hetzner validates the same file at plan time and reports every problem at once, including the ones a schema cannot express.

name.description: Talos cluster name, server-name prefix and the label every resource carries. A DNS-1123 label, because it has to be all three.

domain.description: Public DNS name this environment is reached at. Two or more labels, because a single one is a hostname and not a domain and Let's Encrypt refuses an order for it. Empty or absent until there is one: 40-ingress creates no DNS records and 50-gitops no Ingress, and both say so on every apply.

dnsZone.description: Zone as delegated to Hetzner, when Hetzner holds the authoritative DNS for `domain`. A second field because the zone cut cannot be derived from a name. Empty is supported even with a domain set — the DNS may be hosted anywhere, and 40-ingress then creates no records. `domain` must equal this or be a subdomain of it.

location.description: Object Storage lives in fewer of these than servers do.

networkZone.description: Must contain the location. Derived when omitted; Hetzner rejects a mismatch when the subnet is created, which is late.

nodeSubnet.description: Subnet inside ipRange that nodes address from. Default 10.0.1.0/24.

podCIDR.description: Pod network. Must not overlap ipRange. Default 10.244.0.0/16.

routingMode.description: How pod traffic crosses nodes. native sends it to the private network's gateway, which routes by the per-node routes the hcloud CCM programmes; the machine config carries the route to that gateway. tunnel wraps it in VXLAN between node addresses and needs nothing from that routing, at ~50 bytes a packet. Default native. Switching restarts every Cilium agent, so it is a maintenance operation, not a toggle.

adminCIDRs.description: The only sources allowed to reach tcp/6443 and tcp/50000. MUST include the host running the apply, which pushes Talos machine configuration over the Talos API. No default: an empty list is refused rather than widened to 0.0.0.0/0.

publicIPv4.description: Keep a routable address on every node, and target it from Talos and the kubeconfig. Default TRUE — an apply from outside the private network needs one.

allowICMP.description: Open ping from adminCIDRs. Default false.

version.description: Talos version contract. Must match the baked snapshot: the image lookup keys off this, so bumping without re-baking fails at plan time.

architecture.description: x86 or arm. Decides which image the factory builds, which server types can boot it, and what the serverType fields default to. Switching it needs task cluster:image-bake again: a snapshot is one architecture. Default x86, and arm costs more here, not less.

imageSelector.description: Override the snapshot selector. Empty derives os=talos,talos-version=<version>, the labels cluster:image-bake writes.

version.description: Pinned, not left to Talos: an empty value would let a Talos patch bump move Kubernetes a whole minor with no diff. Default is pinned in pkg/hetzner.

count.description: Odd and positive: etcd needs a quorum, and an even count costs more without tolerating more failures. Default 1.

serverType.description: hcloud server type. Must match talos.architecture or it is refused at plan time. Default follows it: cx23 on x86, cax11 on arm.

apiLoadBalancerType.description: Fronts kube-apiserver. Required once count > 1, ignored otherwise. Default lb11.

workerPools.description: Groups of identically shaped nodes. Omit entirely to schedule on the control plane.

serverType.description: hcloud server type. Default follows talos.architecture: cx33 on x86, cax21 on arm.
